newsitem.title: NORWAY: POLL-ELKEM H1 PRE-TAX SEEN DOWN 15 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLL-ELKEM H1 PRE-TAX SEEN DOWN 15 PCT.

text.p: Six-month pre-tax profits at Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA are expected to fall to around 506 million crowns compared with 598 million crowns in the same period a year ago, a Reuters poll of eight analysts showed.
Two of the analysts recommended buying the stock, three said hold, two said sell and one declined to give a recommendation.

The analysts said the focus would be on prices of Elkem's products now that last year's power crisis in Norway was over and the exchange rate had moved into the positive direction for the export industry.
"It is not certain that ferrosilicon prices will be as high in the time ahead as some believe," said one analyst.
Another analyst said that although prices of steel -- for which ferrosilicon is used in the production -- had climbed, it was not certain that those rises had fed back to producers such as Elkem.
"It is a question of whether Elkem has benefitted from the price increase for siliconmanganese," one analyst said.
He attributed the doubt to Norwegian export statstics, which indicated that producers had achieved lower prices than many analysts had forecast.
Others said they were concerned over fundamentals in Elkem's markets, especially ferrosilicon.
"I think it will be difficult to hold prices up in the future because there will be (competition) problems with exports, especially from Russia," one said.
Another said: "The best arguement against sitting with Elkem shares is that they have risen so much already."
On Friday Elkem was trading 0.50 crowns up at 156 crowns.
"The valuation is way above the fundamental value," said another analyst, who had recommended a sell on the stock.
